chunks: And from his sayings (peace be upon him) he said:

Regarding Marwan ibn al-Hakam at Basrah, they said: Marwan ibn al-Hakam was taken prisoner on the Day of Jamal, so Hasan and Husayn (peace be upon them) interceded for him to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), and they spoke to him about him, so he released him. Then they said to him: 'He desires to swear allegiance to you, O Amir al-Mu'minin?' Whereupon he (peace be upon him) said:

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.مَرْوَانُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ: Marwan ibn al-Hakam, a prominent Umayyad figure
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُلِ: The Day of Jamal (Battle of the Camel)
key_terms.يُبَايِعُكَ: He will swear allegiance to you

ai.seo_question: How did Hasan and Husayn intercede for Marwan ibn al-Hakam's release?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the political pragmatism of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the strategic intercession of his grandsons, Hasan and Husayn (a.s.), who secured Marwan’s release despite his later role in the Umayyad rise. The exchange underscores the early tension between the Ahl al-Bayt’s authority and the emerging Umayyad clan, illustrating how personal loyalty and political calculation intersected in the post-Prophetic era. This event is often cited by Shia scholars to demonstrate the continuity of leadership dynamics within the Prophet’s household during the caliphate of Ali.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Amīr al-mu’minin said about Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam at Baṣrah.

When Marwān was taken prisoner on the day of Jamal, he asked Ḥasan and Ḥusayn (a.s.) to intercede on his behalf before Amīr al-mu’minin. So they spoke to Amīr al-mu’minin about him and he released him. Then they said, “O Amīr al-mu’minin he desires to swear you allegiance” Whereupon Amīr al-mu’minin said :
